title: Junos Configuration Basics: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: In Junos, every setting has exactly one place to live. The configuration is a tree. So you follow the branches, you never guess.

scenes.heading: The menu with pages
scenes.narration: Think of a restaurant menu with different pages for starters, mains and drinks. You write your order, and only then does the kitchen start cooking. Each page is a section of the tree. You write your order on a slip. Handing it to the chef starts the cooking. The chef keeps the last fifty orders.

scenes.heading: A deep example
scenes.narration: Here's how deep the tree can go. This one line sets an address five levels down. Then you check it, commit it, and keep a note for the team. Here's one line five levels deep. Check it first. Then commit it with a note.

lines.t: set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 192.168.1.1/24

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three things to remember. A set command doesn't apply until you commit. Rollback zero doesn't undo a commit, it resets your draft to match the last commit. And the tree goes many levels deep.

items.wrong: A set command applies at once

items.right: It resets the draft to the last commit

items.wrong: Only one level under each section

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva Junos configuration lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. The configuration is a tree, and every setting has one place. Edits go in a draft, and only commit makes them live. Junos keeps the last fifty commits for rollback. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva Junos configuration lab.
